title: Cost and outcome of a budget round
statement: Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over Boolean symbols, let $a,N\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $x$ be a finite schedule-alphabet word. Given any base configuration on $x$, input-head position, integer guide-head coordinate $g$, Boolean word $w$, and guide tape, start the length-only schedule in budget-start phase with the budget head at $|w|+1$ over the captured clock tape for $w$, and the unary head at $N+1$ over the unary tape with $N$ markers. After exactly $2|w|+(a+1)+4$ steps, the budget tape contains the result of a borrow pass with incoming borrow set on $w$, the unary tape has $N+a+1$ markers and its head is at $N+(a+1)+1$, the budget head is at $|w|+1$, and the phase is unary-start if the borrow pass ends with a borrow and budget-start otherwise; the input head, base data, guide tape and guide head are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: schedule input x and base configuration
replaced:
One complete round of the budget controller --- full rewind, append block of $a+1$
unary markers, fixed-width borrow pass, and end test --- costs exactly
$2|w| + (a+1) + 4$ steps, independently of the bits of the budget word $w$.  Starting
in the budget-start phase with budget head at $|w|+1$ over the captured clock tape of
$w$ and unary head at $N+1$ over the unary tape with $N$ markers, the round ends with
the captured clock tape of the borrowed word (incoming borrow set), the unary tape with
$N + a + 1$ markers, and phase unary-start or budget-start according to the borrow's
underflow flag.
